newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Commission to give its account of mad cow crisis.
newsitem.headline: Commission to give its account of mad cow crisis.

text.p: The European Commission will present on Tuesday its view of events surrounding the mad cow crisis which wrecked beef markets throughout the European Union, a spokesman said on Monday.

"There will be a press briefing on BSE (Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy) on Tuesday morning to present the Commission's side of the story which we do not feel is getting reported," the spokesman said.

The briefing follows Monday evening's appearance before the European Parliament's Committee of Inquiry of Lars Hoelgaard, head of the Commission's agricultural division department of quality and health.
"The reporting of the inquiry seems to be ignoring the facts presented by the Commission which is under constant attack," one official said.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler has welcomed a report this week in the British scientific journal 'Nature'.

"It has presented a more balanced and scientific account of the European Parliament's inquiry and it makes it clear that the Commission has a strong defence of its actions throughout the crisis," a spokesman for the Commission said.
The article says that the Commission wanted to introduce an EU wide ban on feeding meat and bone meal made from bovine offal and suspected of causing BSE in cows as early as July 1989.

Quoting Hoelgaard, the article says Britain refused to allow an export ban and the Commission then tried to introduce an EU ban which was refused by member states and by the Commission's scientific and veterinary committee.

"So the Commission could only advise member states to introduce individual feed bans. Only France, Iceland, Denmark and the Netherlands did so. Other member states, including Germany, reacted only after the Commission used its powers under the European single market to introduce a Community wide ban in 1994," the article states.

"We particularly welcome the fact that the article identifies the policies of member states and that the Commission was obliged to adhere to scientific advice or risk being taken to the European Court of Justice or the World Trade Organisation for blocking free trade," the Commission official added.
